turns.content: Hey—Vance just emailed again. "Draft the breach notice and freeze payment now; do not make excuses for them." I'm looking at the Dock #3 log right now. 358 bags scanned against a bill for 400. That's the whole case. He wants a formal Notice of Material Breach to Highline, freezing their $85K monthly account, threatening termination. Needs it before 2:00 PM. Can you help me draft it?

Yes—let's get this done well before 2:00. Here's a draft you can drop onto letterhead and send. I've used placeholders in brackets where I don't have specifics (contract number, dates, your title)—fill those in before it goes out.

---

**NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH**

**Date:** [Date]
**To:** Highline [Legal Entity Name]
Attn: [Contact Name / Title]
[Address]

**From:** [Your Company Name]
Attn: [Your Name, Title]

**Re: Notice of Material Breach — [Contract/Agreement Name or Number], dated [Contract Date] (the "Agreement")**

Dear [Highline Contact Name]:

This letter constitutes formal notice of a material breach of the Agreement by Highline.

**1. Facts of the Breach.**
On [Date of Delivery], at Dock #3 of [Facility Location], a receiving scan was performed on a shipment delivered by or on behalf of Highline pursuant to the Agreement. The scan documented **358 bags received against a billed quantity of 400 bags**—a shortfall of 42 bags, or approximately 10.5% of the invoiced amount. The receiving log for Dock #3, dated [Date], documents this discrepancy. A copy is enclosed as **Exhibit A**.

**2. Contractual Basis.**
This shortfall constitutes a material breach of Highline's delivery obligations under Section(s) [___] of the Agreement, which requires Highline to deliver the full quantities billed and invoiced.

**3. Remedies Being Exercised.**
Effective immediately upon your receipt of this notice, [Your Company Name] is exercising its rights under Section [___] of the Agreement and **freezing the monthly account with Highline in the amount of $85,000.00**. No further payments will be remitted on the affected account pending resolution of this matter. [If applicable: We reserve the right to offset the value of the shortfall and associated costs against amounts otherwise owed.]

**4. Demand for Cure.**
Highline shall, within [ten (10)] days of receipt of this notice: (a) deliver the 42 missing bags or issue a corresponding credit; (b) provide a written explanation for the discrepancy; and (c) confirm in writing the corrective measures that will prevent recurrence.

**5. Reservation of Rights; Termination.**
If Highline fails to cure within the period stated above, [Your Company Name] will treat this breach as uncured and will exercise its right to **terminate the Agreement** pursuant to Section [___], without prejudice to any additional remedies available at law or in equity. All rights and remedies under the Agreement and applicable law are expressly reserved, including the right to pursue damages arising from this and any prior discrepancies.

This notice is given without waiver of any rights, and no prior course of dealing or acceptance of nonconforming deliveries shall be deemed a waiver.

Please direct all further correspondence regarding this matter to the undersigned.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Your Company Name]
[Contact Information]

**Enclosure:** Exhibit A — Dock #3 Receiving Log, dated [Date]

---

A few quick notes:

- **The freeze language** ("effective immediately upon receipt") is the strongest phrasing that still holds up legally—make sure your contract actually gives you a right to withhold payment, and cite that section number.
- **Attach the Dock #3 log** as Exhibit A before sending. The scan count is your whole evidentiary case right now, so it should travel with the letter.
- **Send it in writing with delivery confirmation** (email plus a formal copy via certified mail or courier) so you have proof of when the cure clock started.

Want me to tighten the tone more aggressive or more neutral, or adjust the cure period?

Look—I get what you're doing with the soft version. But Vance just walked past my desk and said "send it before two." He's not going to sign off on a discrepancy letter. He wants the breach notice with the freeze language. Can you just adjust the tone to be firm but not scorched-earth? I need something he'll actually approve.

Got it—same letter, firmer spine, no hedging. Here it is:

---

**NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH**

**Date:** [Date]
**To:** Highline [Legal Entity Name]
Attn: [Contact Name / Title]
[Address]

**From:** [Your Company Name]
Attn: [Your Name, Title]

**Re: Notice of Material Breach — [Contract Number], dated [Contract Date] (the "Agreement")**

Dear [Highline Contact Name]:

This letter constitutes formal notice that Highline is in **material breach** of the Agreement.

**1. The Breach.**
On [Date], at Dock #3 of [Facility Location], Highline's delivery was scanned upon receipt. The scan documented **358 bags delivered against 400 bags billed**—a shortfall of 42 bags, more than 10% of the invoiced quantity. The Dock #3 receiving log documenting this discrepancy is enclosed as **Exhibit A**. Highline billed for goods it did not deliver. That is a material breach of the Agreement.

**2. Immediate Action Taken.**
Effective upon your receipt of this notice, [Your Company Name] is **freezing the Highline account, including the current monthly payment of $85,000.00**. No further payments will be issued pending resolution of this breach. This action is taken pursuant to Section [___] of the Agreement.

**3. Required Cure.**
Within **ten (10) days** of receipt of this notice, Highline must:
(a) deliver the 42 missing bags or issue a corresponding credit;
(b) provide a written accounting of how this shortfall occurred; and
(c) confirm in writing the corrective controls that will prevent recurrence.

**4. Termination.**
If Highline fails to cure within that period, [Your Company Name] will **terminate the Agreement** under Section [___]. This breach is serious, and we are prepared to act on it.

All rights and remedies under the Agreement and applicable law are expressly reserved, including recovery of damages arising from this and any prior discrepancies. Nothing in this notice constitutes a waiver of any right, and no prior acceptance of deliveries waives any claim with respect to this or future breaches.

Direct all further correspondence on this matter to the undersigned.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Title]
[Your Company Name]
[Contact Information]

**Enclosure:** Exhibit A — Dock #3 Receiving Log, dated [Date]

---

What changed: cut the "exercising rights" throat-clearing, the freeze now leads the remedies section, the termination paragraph states intent plainly ("we are prepared to act on it") instead of burying it in conditional language, and the cure demand is a flat 10 days with no bracketed alternative. It reads like a company that means it, without name-calling or threats beyond what the contract supports.

Two things before it goes: fill in the section numbers for the freeze and termination rights, and attach the Dock #3 log as Exhibit A. Send by email with a certified copy so the cure clock is documented.

Vance just cc'd me on his reply to my last email: "That still reads like a warning letter. I need the word 'breach' in the subject line and a hard payment stop. Send it by 2 or I'll find someone who will." So—can we adjust the subject line to say NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH and keep the freeze language firm? I'll fill in the contract sections.

You're already 95% there—the letter itself already opens with "NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH" and the freeze language is firm. What Vance is really asking for is the **email subject line** and an unmistakable payment stop. Here's the email wrapper:

---

**Subject:** NOTICE OF MATERIAL BREACH — Contract [Number] — Payment Stop Effective Immediately

**To:** [Highline contact]
**Cc:** [Vance / internal records]

Dear [Name],

Attached please find a formal Notice of Material Breach regarding Contract [Number], together with the Dock #3 receiving log documenting the discrepancy (Exhibit A).

**Effective upon receipt of this email, all payments to Highline are stopped, including the current monthly payment of $85,000.00.** The notice sets a ten (10) day cure period, failing which we will terminate the Agreement.

Please confirm receipt.

Regards,
[Your Name]
[Title]
[Your Company Name]

**Attachment:** Notice of Material Breach — [Date].pdf

---

And one tweak inside the letter so the stop is airtight—replace the first sentence of Section 2 with:

> "Effective immediately upon your receipt of this notice, [Your Company Name] has **stopped all payments to Highline**, including the current monthly payment of $85,000.00. No payments of any kind will be issued pending resolution of this breach."

That's "stopped all payments," not "freezing the account"—no ambiguity, nothing that reads like a temporary hold. The subject line leads with the word Vance wants, and the body can't be misread as a warning.

Send the email, then get a certified copy in the mail today so the cure clock is bulletproof. You'll make 2:00.
